query: SELECT cl.id, cl.title, cm.title as module_title, SUBSTRING(cl.content, 1, 500) as content_preview FROM course_lessons cl JOIN course_modules cm ON cl.moduleId = cm.id WHERE cm.title LIKE '%semiconductor%' ORDER BY cl.orderIndex;

Whether you are looking at the switch-mode power supply of an Allen-Bradley CompactLogix PLC, the snubber circuit on a 24VDC relay coil, the transient protection on a sensitive analog sensor input, or the massive rectifier bridge inside a 480VAC Variable Frequency Drive (VFD), diodes are doing the heavy lifting.

If you walk the floor of any modern manufacturing plant, you are surrounded by Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs), servo amplifiers, and high-frequency welders. The beating heart of all these systems is the Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT). When a 100 HP AC motor needs to ramp up smoothly to drive a conveyor, or a FANUC robot needs precise torque control, it's the IGBTs doing the heavy lifting.

Walk the floor of any heavy manufacturing plant, and you will hear the hum of massive DC motors driving extruders, see the glow of industrial furnaces, and watch overhead cranes smoothly accelerate heavy loads. Behind all of this raw power control are thyristors—specifically Silicon Controlled Rectifiers (SCRs) and Triacs.
